_doc: The single registry of every recursive-self-improvement loop in SYNAPSE. Reconciles the June 2026 six-line harness (docs/rsi/) with the July 2026 read-only audit (harness/notes/RSI_SURFACE_AUDIT.md). A loop's rung is the highest rung for which EVERY rung below is also proven -- rungs_proven is a contiguous prefix, never a cherry-pick. 'human_ratified' is flipped by a HUMAN only; an agent may propose any rung and flip none above L3.

ladder.L0: EXISTS -- the mechanism is present in code
ladder.L1: HONEST -- its input signal CAN represent failure
ladder.L2: REACHABLE -- a live non-test path constructs and drives it
ladder.L3: CONSUMED -- something reads its output AND a later decision differs
ladder.L4: DURABLE -- the effect survives a real process restart (two-run proof)
ladder.L5: BENEFICIAL -- a task-outcome metric moved, measured before AND after

_ladder_collision_warning: The June harness (docs/rsi/SPEC.md) ALSO used L0-L4 with DIFFERENT semantics: its L2 meant 'survives a real restart' (this ladder's L4) and its L3 meant 'alters a later decision' (this ladder's L3). June closure claims are therefore NOT directly importable. Every june-harness loop below starts at rungs_proven=[] and must be re-derived by Line A. This collision is the single largest reconciliation hazard in the harness.

verification_legend.verified-at-head: re-confirmed against working-tree code at frame_commit during this frame
verification_legend.audit-cited: asserted by RSI_SURFACE_AUDIT.md with a probe; not personally re-run this frame
verification_legend.unverified: carried from a prior effort or memory; Line A must establish it

loops.name: EpochAdapter -- router tier-threshold adaptation
loops.blocker: L1 CLOSED 2026-08-01; CORRECTED the same day (RL-2b) after a crucible pass caught the first closure overclaiming its own reach. _record_metric's `success` parameter is REQUIRED -- no default -- at router.py:1019, and all TEN call sites pass a real outcome: router.py:297 (cache), :390 (no-tier fallback, literal False), :466 and :533 (recipe/plan), :578 (tier 0), :620 (tier 1), :745 (tier 2), :850 and :863 (tier-3 worker failure paths), :921 (tier-3 sync success). WHAT THE FIRST PASS MISSED: plumbing result.success through every call site is not honesty if the RoutingResult's own success is itself a literal. _try_tier3 built success=True and recorded it AT LAUNCH (old :765), before the background worker had produced any outcome; the worker's real verdict, stored into _async_results milliseconds to minutes later, never entered the sample. Every async DEEP route scored 1.0 regardless of how it ended. Corrected by option (c) of defer / provisional-then-amend / do-not-record-at-launch: _try_tier3 (router.py:752-806) records NOTHING at launch, and _tier3_worker (router.py:808-864) records the outcome it actually observes -- False on the raised path and False on the _tier3_sync-returned-None path, with the success path left to _tier3_sync's own record at :921 so one route yields exactly one DEEP sample. Deferring to get_async_result() was rejected because it POPs, so an unpolled handle would never be sampled at all and worker latency would be attributed to the poller; record-then-amend was rejected because EpochAdapter.record (adaptation.py:138-143) appends into a rotating fixed-size deque with no amend API, so a provisional True can be aggregated into a threshold before its correction arrives. L2 REACHABLE is the blocker, and the PRIOR TEXT FOR IT WAS FALSE AND IS RETRACTED. It read: 'L2 needs live routed traffic through TieredRouter -- not another code change.' The real obstacle is two facts, and the first of them IS a code change: (1) THE PRODUCTION ROUTER IS CONSTRUCTED WITHOUT A command_fn. python/synapse/server/handlers.py:1625 is the ONLY non-test TieredRouter construction in the repository -- a tree-wide grep for 'TieredRouter(' over *.py, excluding tests/, returns exactly that one line -- and it passes config=config only. command_fn defaults to None (router.py:173). With it None, tier 0's execution branch (if self._command_fn and parse.command:) and tier 2's (if self._command_fn:) can never run, so responses is permanently empty and all(r.success for r in responses) is permanently all([]) == True. The corrected tier-0/tier-2 signal is UNREACHABLE from the live path, not merely un-exercised: traffic alone cannot exercise it, because a router with no command channel cannot execute a command and so can never observe one fail. (2) THE ROUTER HAS RECORDED ZERO PRODUCTION REQUESTS. synapse_live_metrics against a live bridge (synapse_ping -> pong=true, protocol 4.0.0) on 2026-08-01 returned routing.total_requests=0 with tier_counts=[]. L2 therefore needs BOTH a command_fn wired at handlers.py:1625 AND live traffic through it. Wiring the command channel is a signal-semantics change and sits behind the human gate.

L1: python/synapse/routing/router.py:937-962 -- _record_metric(tier: Union[RoutingTier, str], latency_ms: float, success: bool). `success` is REQUIRED, no default: a forgetful future call site is now a TypeError, not a silent 1.0. `tier` accepts a bare str so a no-tier outcome can enter the sample.
python/synapse/routing/router.py:293, :462, :529, :574, :604, :729, :765, :839 -- all eight tier call sites pass result.success (previously all eight passed only (tier, latency)).
python/synapse/routing/router.py:386 -- the no_tier_matched fallback now records (NO_TIER_KEY, latency, False). It previously recorded nothing, so genuine failures never entered the sample.
python/synapse/routing/router.py:557 -- _try_tier0 success = all(r.success for r in responses), replacing the hardcoded success=True.
python/synapse/routing/router.py:713 -- _try_tier2 same correction (structurally identical defect, fixed in the same commit for consistency).

tests/test_routing.py::TestRewardSignalHonesty -- 10 tests asserting on router._epoch._current_epoch.outcomes, i.e. what the ADAPTER was told, not what RoutingResult claimed: raising command_fn -> False; returned-failure response -> False; tier-0 result.success False AND adapter told False; no-tier-matched -> exactly one failure record keyed NO_TIER_KEY; success path still True (paired positive control); a mixed run yields BOTH values; a parse-only route is not a failure (overcorrection guard); `success` has no default (structural ratchet); every call site passes an outcome (source-level mirror of verify.py P4).

tests/test_routing.py::TestTieredRouter::test_tier0_command_fn_error -- rewritten: it previously asserted result.success on the grounds that 'routing succeeded even if execution failed', which is the assertion that pinned the defect.

mutation-verified 2026-08-01 -- three mutants, each killed by the intended tests: (A) restore tier-0 success=True -> 4 failed; (B) delete the fallback _record_metric -> 2 failed; (C) restore `success: bool = True` and silence one call site -> 6 failed.
harness/rsi/verify.py P4 live grep at this commit: '9/9 call sites pass an outcome (lines 293, 386, 462, 529, 574, 604, 729, 765)'.

safety fact verified BEFORE landing: TierThresholds.get() has zero non-test callers -- grep -rn 'TierThresholds' and '.thresholds.get' over python/ shared/ tests/ returns only adaptation.py itself, the routing/__init__.py re-export, and tests/test_v5_features.py. Both stats consumers (server/live_metrics.py:269, server/metrics.py:62) iterate tiers.items() generically, so the new 'no_tier' key is a labelled series, not a KeyError.

RL-2b CORRECTION 2026-08-01 -- router.py:752-806 _try_tier3 no longer calls _record_metric at launch; router.py:808-864 _tier3_worker records the outcome it actually observes (False on raise at :863, False on _tier3_sync-returned-None at :850, success left to _tier3_sync's own record at :921 so one route yields exactly one DEEP sample). Both failure paths now also STORE a RoutingResult, so a dead async route's handle resolves instead of leaving a poller waiting forever.

REFUTED, not fixed -- router.py:588-600 (_try_tier1) and :874-883 (_tier3_sync) hold success=True literals that are CORRECT: neither tier touches command_fn or populates responses, so all(r.success for r in responses) would be all([]) -- a literal True wearing a costume. Truth contracts documented inline at both sites. router.py:243-252 (the conversational short-circuit) is refuted for a different reason: it returns before any _record_metric or _cache_result call, so it is outside the reward sample entirely and cannot pin any series.

tests/test_routing.py::TestAsyncDeepSignalHonesty -- 5 tests reading _epoch._current_epoch.outcomes: launch records no outcome; worker exception -> False; worker None-result -> False AND the handle resolves; success control records exactly ONE True (guards vacuity and double-counting at once); a mixed run yields BOTH values.

tests/test_routing.py::TestRefutedConstantSites -- 3 tests pinning the refutations so a later pass cannot 'fix' a line that was already truthful: the conversational path is outside the sample; a seeded cache hit replays a False; a repeated failing route is served by the TIER PIN (route() checks pins at step 0, before the cache at step 0.5), not by the cache.

mutation-verified 2026-08-01 (RL-2b) -- mutant A, restore the launch-time _record_metric: killed by test_async_launch_records_no_outcome (1 failed). Mutant B, silence both worker failure records: killed by test_worker_exception_is_recorded_as_failure, test_worker_none_result_is_recorded_as_failure and test_deep_series_carries_both_values (3 failed).

L2 OBSTACLE, verified at this commit -- python/synapse/server/handlers.py:1625 constructs TieredRouter(config=config) with NO command_fn (default None, router.py:173), and it is the only non-test construction in the tree. Tier 0 and tier 2 gate their execution on self._command_fn, so neither can execute in production and neither can observe a failure there.

harness/rsi/verify.py P4 live grep at this commit: '10/10 call sites pass an outcome (lines 297, 390, 466, 533, 578, 620, 745, 850)'. The printed list truncates at 8; the full set is 297, 390, 466, 533, 578, 620, 745, 850, 863, 921.

loops.danger_if_closed_now: LOW at L1 -- but the honesty CLAIM has to be SCOPED, because an overstated honesty claim is itself the failure this rung exists to prevent, and the first pass made one. 'The signal can now represent failure' was true of the INSTANT, STANDARD, RECIPE and no_tier series and FALSE of FAST and DEEP, which were still pinned to 1.0 by a literal success=True. State as the code now stands: DEEP CAN carry False -- an async route that dies records False from _tier3_worker (router.py:850, :863), pinned both ways by tests/test_routing.py::TestAsyncDeepSignalHonesty. CACHE was never pinned -- the cache-hit result is built with success=cached.success, not a literal; note also that cache.py's _DEFAULT_TTLS gives 'recipe' and 'instant' a TTL of 0, so ResponseCache.put returns early and only fast/standard/deep are cacheable at all. FAST REMAINS STRUCTURALLY 1.0 and was deliberately NOT changed: _try_tier1 (router.py:581-621) never touches command_fn and never populates responses, and it reaches _record_metric only on its success path -- its not-found / low-confidence exit is `return None`, which is a CASCADE decision rather than a tier-1 failure (the request continues to tier 2 and may succeed there; scoring it as a FAST failure would count one request twice, in two series). Total routing failure is already sampled under NO_TIER_KEY. Anyone reading tier success rates must know that FAST's 1.0 is definitional, not evidence -- that is the live residual risk of this rung, and it is documented rather than fixed. Nothing consumes any of it today: TierThresholds.get() has ZERO non-test callers, re-verified at this commit. The CRITICAL danger still belongs to L3 CONSUMED, not L1 -- wiring TierThresholds.get() into the cascade converts a decorative mechanism into a live one-way ratchet with no persistence, no versioning and no rollback. The audit's P4 probe drove 300 outcomes and measured a monotonic slide to the 0.10 clamp floor in eight epochs, then flat for the life of the process -- but that probe ran against the CONSTANT signal. With DEEP unpinned the ratchet direction is no longer predetermined, which is a precondition for consumption and not a substitute for the reversal work in `reversal`.
loops.reversal_note: adaptation.py:121-126 -- no disk read, no disk write, always starts at epoch_id=0 with thresholds={}. Bounded only by deque(maxlen=100) and the [0.1, 1.0] clamp. De-facto reversal is process restart, which is amnesia rather than rollback.

loops.name: section-16 observability -- RecommendationHistory into agent health
loops._surface_note: shared/conductor_advisor.py is the read side of this loop -- it consumes LosslessExecutionBridge.operation_stats(), MOERouter fingerprint counts, and LosslessEvolution's EvolutionIntegrity failure list, and emits Recommendations. shared/evolution.py (LosslessEvolution, markdown->USD, EvolutionIntegrity) is one of those data sources and is a DIFFERENT module from python/synapse/memory/evolution.py, which is loop A3's superseded charmander/charmeleon path. Both were added after the P1 sweep caught them unregistered at frame time.
loops.blocker: L1 HONEST is unproven -- not refuted, simply never checked, by June or by this pass. The June wiring SURVIVES at HEAD: RecommendationHistory is defined at shared/conductor_advisor.py:363, exported at shared/__init__.py:59,:110, and imported by a real non-test caller at python/synapse/panel/agent_health.py:35. loops.name: router fast-path session promotion
loops._surface_note: shared/constants.py holds FAST_PATHS and FAST_PATH_PROMOTION_THRESHOLD -- the promotion threshold and the CONSTANTS_HASH that stamps session fast paths. Added after the P1 sweep caught it unregistered at frame time.
loops.blocker: Two independent obstacles, and the L1 one is the newly-identified and more serious. (1) L1: promotion is driven by fingerprint FREQUENCY -- MOERouter.route() increments a per-fingerprint counter and auto-promotes at FAST_PATH_PROMOTION_THRESHOLD (default 3), stamped with CONSTANTS_HASH. Frequency cannot represent failure: a fingerprint that fails every single time is promoted identically to one that always succeeds. This loop inherits A1's constant-success blindness at the routing layer. (2) L4: _session_fast_paths is in-memory only and dies with the process. Both claims need Line A confirmation against HEAD -- CLAUDE.md section 2.3 is the doc source, not a verification.
loops.danger_if_closed_now: HIGH if only the persistence half is addressed. Persisting a frequency-promoted fast-path table across restarts would make a failure-blind promotion permanent instead of process-scoped -- strictly worse than today. Fix L1 before L4. This loop is the clearest illustration of why this harness exists.
loops.reversal_note: Process restart clears _session_fast_paths today. CONSTANTS_HASH stamping means keyword-table drift invalidates stamped entries, which is an invalidation mechanism, not a rollback.

loops.name: FORGE build loop -- fix application and validation counters
loops.blocker: L1 CLOSED 2026-08-01 (RL-2 SIGNAL), corrected the same day after a crucible pass. The prior blocker was: orchestrator.py:177 `fixes_applied += 1  # Optimistic`, orchestrator.py:214 `fixes_validated=0,  # Set after verification phase`, and reporter.py:65 RENDERING that hardcoded zero to a human as `Validated: {metrics.fixes_validated}` -- a constant displayed as a measurement. FIRST QUESTION ANSWERED: no verification phase exists in forge/engine. `FORGE.md` Phase 5 ('VERIFY (Re-run)') is a procedure a human or Claude Code follows, not a module -- grep over forge/ found no apply/verify/re-run function and no runnable entry point, confirming the 2026-06-05 CTO finding. The :214 comment's claimed 'verification phase' was therefore a phantom. Taken the HONEST-REPORTING branch rather than fabricating a validator: fixes_validated is now `None` (the 'unvalidated' sentinel) unless real FixOutcome re-run evidence produced a number, reporter.py renders the word `unvalidated` and never a numeral without a measurement, and a displayed 0 now means only 'validation ran and confirmed nothing'. fixes_applied is derived from confirmed-application evidence and no longer increments on classification. CRUCIBLE CORRECTION: the first pass left a SURVIVING MUTANT at its own defect site -- flipping metrics.py:44 back to `fixes_validated: int | None = 0` passed ALL FIFTEEN of the original tests, because not one of them called MetricsTracker.compute_cycle_metrics; they exercised the CycleMetrics dataclass default (schemas.py:420) and the orchestrator above it, never the tracker entry point in between. Four new tests now kill that mutant, proven RED-then-GREEN by flipping the default in both directions. L1 bar met in the 'honest unvalidated' direction: the signal CAN represent failure -- an applied fix whose re-run refutes it (FixOutcome(applied=True, validated=False)) lowers the count, and an all-refuted cycle yields a MEASURED 0 that is distinguishable from the unmeasured sentinel (test_all_reruns_failing_yields_a_measured_zero_not_the_sentinel)

known_limits: UNBOUNDED SELF-ASSERTION (crucible finding, DEFERRED with reasoning): process_results accepts any FixOutcome list and cross-checks none of it. Deferred deliberately -- there is nothing in forge/engine to cross-check against (no apply stage, no re-run stage, no execution surface of any kind), so any check the engine could perform would be another self-assertion in a different costume; the caller writes scenario_id, applied AND validated. What the fix does guarantee is narrower and real: the engine no longer manufactures counts on its OWN authority, and every count is now attributable to a caller who claimed it. Closing this needs a real verifier that re-runs the scenario and reads the result -- the same missing apply/verify stage that blocks L2. Named explicitly in the FixOutcome docstring (schemas.py:348-360) so the type is not mistaken for a verification boundary.
loops.danger_if_closed_now: HIGH at L2+. June called this 'the ONE large build'. The L1 fix removes the fabricated success value but does NOT build an apply/verify stage -- FORGE still cannot improve itself, it can now only report that fact honestly. Driving this loop live (L2) without first building a real apply+re-run stage would compound unvalidated fixes: the exact hazard in the harness-updating-is-not-harness-benefit lens. Benefit without verification is a hazard, not a win.
loops.reversal_note: Counters persist to forge/metrics/cycles.json (append-only list, no schema version). CORRECTED 2026-08-01 (crucible finding): the three historical cycles carried `fixes_validated: 0` and are NOW rewritten to `null`. The earlier text here said they were deliberately left alone as pre-fix records -- that was wrong under the new contract, where a rendered 0 asserts 'a re-run ran and confirmed nothing'. loops.name: convergence -- two-tier Moneta substrate (subtractive)
loops.blocker: Not a dormant loop but the substrate the other loops converge onto, and it is SUBTRACTIVE by design: delete the bespoke append-logs and repoint at Moneta. Moneta is built and importable (moneta_runtime.moneta_available() returns True) but default-OFF -- store.py:810 reads SYNAPSE_MEMORY_BACKEND with a jsonl default, and the variable is unset on this machine. A confounder found by the audit: .synapse/config.yaml:17 says memory_backend: 'flat', a DIFFERENT key that the store selector never reads, so it neither selects moneta nor changes the backend and must not be mistaken for configuration.
loops.danger_if_closed_now: MEDIUM. Flipping the backend default relocates every other loop's persistence substrate at once. Sequence it after the L1 fixes, not before, or the signal work lands on a substrate that is about to move.
loops.reversal_note: SYNAPSE_MEMORY_BACKEND is a genuine reversal lever -- flipping it back restores jsonl -- but data written under one backend is not automatically migrated to the other.
